nodes.summary: For groups $T$ and $G$, the group $G$ lies in the class $\mathfrak{F}_T$ when it has a subnormal series $1 = H_0 \le H_1 \le \dots \le H_n = G$, each $H_i$ normal in $H_{i+1}$, all of whose factors $H_{i+1}/H_i$ are isomorphic to $T$. For simple $T$ these are the groups all of whose composition factors are isomorphic to $T$.
nodes.title: Groups with a subnormal series whose factors are all isomorphic to a given group

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a finite non-abelian simple group, and write $\mathfrak{F}_T$ for the class of groups having a subnormal series all of whose factors are isomorphic to $T$. Let $\mathfrak{M}$ and $\mathfrak{H}$ be formations whose finite members lie in $\mathfrak{F}_T$, each containing a nontrivial finite group and each missing some finite group of $\mathfrak{F}_T$. Then it is not true that, for every finite group $G$,…
nodes.title: Mel'nikov's theorem on Kourovka Problem 12.97

nodes.summary: For a group $T$, write $\mathfrak{F}_T$ for the class of groups having a subnormal series all of whose factors are isomorphic to $T$. This is the proposition that, for every finite non-abelian simple group $T$ and all formations $\mathfrak{M}$ and $\mathfrak{H}$ whose finite members lie in $\mathfrak{F}_T$, each containing a nontrivial finite group and each missing some finite group of $\mathfrak{F}_T$, it is not…
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 12.97 (Shemetkov)

nodes.summary: A class of groups is given by a membership predicate on groups such that every group isomorphic to a member is again a member. Only the finite members matter in the formulation of Kourovka Problem 12.97.
nodes.title: Isomorphism-closed classes of groups (Kourovka 12.97)

nodes.summary: A class of finite groups is given by a membership predicate: a proposition $X(G)$ for every finite group $G$. It is not required to be closed under isomorphisms.
nodes.title: Class of finite groups (Kourovka 10.72)

nodes.summary: A class $X$ of groups is a formation when it contains the trivial group, the quotient $G/N$ lies in $X$ for every finite group $G$ in $X$ and every normal subgroup $N$ of $G$, and for every finite group $G$ with normal subgroups $N_1$ and $N_2$ such that $G/N_1$ and $G/N_2$ lie in $X$, the quotient $G/(N_1 \cap N_2)$ lies in $X$.
nodes.title: Formations of finite groups (Kourovka 12.97)

nodes.summary: A class $X$ of finite groups is a formation when it is closed under isomorphisms, contains the trivial group, contains the quotient $G/N$ of each of its members $G$ by every normal subgroup $N$, and contains $G/(N_1 \cap N_2)$ whenever $N_1$ and $N_2$ are normal subgroups of a finite group $G$ with $G/N_1$ and $G/N_2$ in $X$. The last condition is closure under subdirect products.
nodes.title: Formation of finite groups (Kourovka 10.72)

nodes.summary: `X` is a proper subclass of `𝔉_T`: some finite group of `𝔉_T` does not belong to `X`.
nodes.title: Proper subclass of a formation

nodes.summary: A class $X$ of groups is nontrivial when it contains a nontrivial finite group; for a formation this means that $X$ is not the trivial formation.
nodes.title: Classes containing a nontrivial finite group

nodes.summary: For every prime $p$, the class $\mathfrak{N}_p$ of all finite $p$-groups is not the Gaschütz product $\mathfrak{F} \circ \mathfrak{G}$ of two formations $\mathfrak{F}$ and $\mathfrak{G}$ that consist of $p$-groups, each contain a nontrivial group and each omit some finite $p$-group. Here a finite group $G$ lies in $\mathfrak{F} \circ \mathfrak{G}$ when its $\mathfrak{G}$-residual lies in $\mathfrak{F}$.
nodes.title: The formation of finite $p$-groups is indecomposable

nodes.summary: The statement that for every prime $p$, the class $\mathfrak{N}_p$ of all finite $p$-groups is not the Gaschütz product $\mathfrak{F} \circ \mathfrak{G}$ of two formations $\mathfrak{F}$ and $\mathfrak{G}$ that consist of $p$-groups, each contain a nontrivial group and each omit some finite $p$-group. Here a finite group $G$ lies in $\mathfrak{F} \circ \mathfrak{G}$ when its $\mathfrak{G}$-residual lies in…
nodes.title: Indecomposability of the formation of finite $p$-groups (Kourovka 10.72)

nodes.summary: For a class $X$ of groups and a group $G$, the $X$-residual of $G$ is the intersection of all normal subgroups $N$ of $G$ such that the quotient $G/N$ lies in $X$.
nodes.title: The residual of a group with respect to a class (Kourovka 12.97)

nodes.summary: For a class $X$ of finite groups and a finite group $G$, the $X$-residual of $G$ is the intersection of all normal subgroups $N$ of $G$ with $G/N \in X$. When $X$ is a formation, it is the smallest such $N$.
nodes.title: Residual of a finite group with respect to a class (Kourovka 10.72)

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
